input.raw_text: I've been at this desk since dinnertime and I still don't have my bearings. Futures hit their down limit — five percent, locked, no bids worth speaking of — as the Florida and North Carolina counts came in, and the peso collapsed close to ten percent. Now, with the map tilting decisively to Trump, we are violently reversing: S&P futures have cut the loss to barely a percent, Nasdaq futures have gone green, and yields are ripping off the lows with the ten-year back above 1.80%. Banks are being bid hard on reflation talk while the Mexican peso is still reeling. This is one of the fastest sentiment flips I have ever traded through — the crowd pricing a safe-haven crash an hour ago is now buying the dip.
input.summary: An extreme election-linked risk-off move reversed rapidly as US equity futures recovered, Nasdaq futures turned positive, Treasury yields rebounded, and bank equities strengthened on reflation expectations, while the Mexican peso remained sharply weaker. The speed and divergence of the moves reflected unusually high volatility and unsettled sentiment.

citations.text: Regime-conditional return distribution shift in international equity returns: normal regime characterized by mean monthly return ~0.90% and volatility ~2.81%; bear regime characterized by mean monthly return ~0.13% (near zero) and volatility ~5.04% (~80% higher than normal). Observable as a bimodal or multi-modal return distribution when regimes are mixed, with the bear component dominating the left tail. Filtered regime probabilities from the Hamilton filter provide the real-time signal for which regime parameter set is active. Estimated at monthly frequency on world equity index data (MLE, Ang-Bekaert 2004 Tables 2-3). regime_conditional_mean_return; regime_conditional_return_volatility; filtered_regime_probability; bear_regime_volatility_ratio The ~80% higher bear-regime volatility (5.04% vs. 2.81%) and near-zero bear mean (0.13% vs. 0.90%) are the key quantitative observables. These parameter values provide calibration anchors for regime detection models applied to international equity markets.

matched_states.state_summary: A two-state Markov-switching market condition for international equity returns characterized by empirically estimated regime-level parameters: normal regime (monthly mean μ=0.90%, volatility σ=2.81%) and bear regime (monthly mean μ=0.13%, volatility σ=5.04%). The bear regime exhibits approximately 80% higher volatility and near-zero mean returns relative to the normal regime. Transition probabilities govern regime persistence; the Hamilton filter provides real-time probability estimates of the active regime. Estimated on world equity index data at monthly frequency (Ang and Bekaert 2004, Tables 2-3).
matched_states.title: Two-State International Equity Regime State (Normal / Bear Parameters)

citations.text: The filtered probability distribution across three hidden Markov model states (bull, bear, high-volatility) estimated from EWMM features of daily futures returns. The observation vector per instrument is the concatenation of EWMM first moment (mean) and second moment (variance) of returns, normalized and processed independently per asset class. The three regime states correspond to distinct return-volatility configurations: bull (positive expected return, moderate volatility), bear (negative or near-zero expected return, elevated volatility), and high-volatility (extreme variance). The HMM filter produces real-time posterior state probability estimates that can be read as continuous regime indicators. Applied uniformly to 15 futures instruments (4 commodity, 4 currency, 4 equity, 3 fixed income; 4972 daily observations Jan 2000 – Oct 2019). Three states selected via greedy model selection (Nguyen 2021). hmm_filtered_state_probability_bull; hmm_filtered_state_probability_bear; hmm_filtered_state_probability_high_vol; ewmm_return_mean; ewmm_return_variance The asset-independent design is a key feature: the same HMM framework applies to commodity, currency, equity, and fixed income futures without modification. EWMM span parameter controls responsiveness (lower span = faster regime detection but higher turnover; span=30 recommended). Three-state structure identified via greedy approach; alternative state counts were not systematically validated.

matched_states.state_summary: A three-state hidden Markov model (HMM) regime structure applied asset- independently to daily futures returns across commodity, currency, equity, and fixed income classes. The three states are labeled bull (positive return, moderate volatility), bear (negative or flat return, elevated volatility), and high-volatility (extreme variance). The model uses EWMM (exponentially weighted moving moment) features of first and second return moments, normalized and concatenated independently per instrument, as the observation vector. Applied uniformly to 15 futures instruments (4 commodity, 4 currency, 4 equity, 3 fixed income) using 4972 daily observations (January 2000 – October 2019). Three states selected via greedy model selection. The PESR metric (Predicted Expected Sharpe Ratio) translates HMM-predicted state probabilities into a forward-looking scalar risk-adjusted return forecast by combining state-level SR estimates with h-step-ahead transition matrix powers. OOS long-only strategy (Jan 2016 – Oct 2019) achieves substantially higher Sharpe ratios than buy-and-hold across most instruments at 5bps transaction costs (e.g., EQ4: SR=3.0 vs. 1.0 B&H). EWMM span=30 provides a favorable SR/turnover tradeoff (Nguyen 2021 preprint).
matched_states.title: Three-State HMM Market Regime (Bull / Bear / High-Volatility)

citations.text: Volatility clustering in financial return time series: significant positive autocorrelation in squared returns (|r_t|^2) and absolute returns (|r_t|) at short to medium lags, indicating that large-magnitude returns tend to cluster in time. Measured by the Ljung-Box Q-statistic on squared residuals and the autocorrelation function (ACF) of squared returns. In GARCH(1,1) terms, high persistence (delta close to 1, alpha+delta near 1) produces slow mean-reversion of conditional variance after shocks. Observable as extended runs of high-volatility or low-volatility trading days in any major financial return series. squared_return_autocorrelation; absolute_return_autocorrelation; ljung_box_q_stat_squared_residuals; garch_persistence_parameter_sum Foundational observable motivating GARCH modeling. The ACF of squared returns (not raw returns) is the primary diagnostic; raw returns are approximately uncorrelated while squared returns exhibit significant autocorrelation. This distinguishes GARCH effects from mean autocorrelation.

matched_states.state_summary: A market condition characterized by persistent clustering of return volatility— large shocks followed by further large shocks and small shocks followed by further small shocks—captured by a GARCH(1,1) conditional variance process h_t = omega + alpha * u_{t-1}^2 + delta * h_{t-1}. High persistence (alpha + delta near 1, delta close to 1) implies slow mean-reversion of conditional variance following a shock, producing extended periods of elevated or depressed volatility. The state is active whenever GARCH persistence parameters are large and squared-return autocorrelations are significant.
matched_states.title: GARCH Volatility Clustering Persistence State
